page.layout: One column of running text in Latin with Arabic quotations; notes in the left margin; a small-type block of Arabic and Latin below the text. Printed page number and running head at the top; catchword at the lower right.

main_text.p: rum alia alios infidelitatis arguant, teste Authore libri Id. & AlSharestani. Al Mawakef. Porrò ipsi se اصحاب العدل والتوحيد Æquitatis & unitatis [Dei] propugnatores, nuncupant, ab aliis autem يلقبون بالقدرية cognominantur AlKadarii, quanquam hoc nomen uni apud ipsos sectæ peculiare statuat Gregorius noster.

Illud de quo inter eos in universum convenit, hoc est, quod attributa aeterna ab essentia Creatoris amoveant] Ita & illud in quod universi conspirant describit Alsharestanius; فالذي يعم طايفة المعتزلة من الاعتقاد القول بان الله تعالى قديم والقدم اخص وصف ذاته ونفوا الصفات القديمة اصلا فقالوا هو عالم لذاته قادر لذاته حي لذاته لا بعلم وقدرة وحياة هي صفات قديمة ومعان قايمة به لاذاته لو شاركت الصفات في القدم الذي هو اخص الوصف لشاركته في الالهية &c.Communis totius Motazalorum gentis confessio hæc est, Deum esse æternum, & æternitatem attributum essentiæ ejus maximè proprium esse; & quod attributa aeterna penitus rejiciant, dicentes Deum omniscium esse per essentiam suam, [vel per se] potentem per essentiam suam, viventè per essentiâ suâ,* Maimon des rotunde, sed ex sua non Mota-zalorum sententia . Deum esse موجود non per scientiam, potentiam aut vitam, quæ sint attributa æterna, & significatus in ipso subsistentes: quoniam si cum eo participarent attributa in æternitate quæ attributum maximè pro-

لا موجود وحي لا بحياة وقادر لا بقدرة وعالم لا بعلم بل الكل راجع لمعنى واحد لا تكثير فيه Morch. l.1, c. 57. (cf. existentem sed non per existentiam: & vivere, sed non per vitam: & potentem, esse sed non per potentiam: & scire, sed non per scientiam, sed omnia in unum redire significatum, in quo nulla est mu'ltiplicitas.

page.notes: The Arabic lines are copied from a small scan; the vowel-less words of the first two lines and the final Arabic line are doubtful and may contain errors. The text "Deum omniscium" is printed as such. The marginal note marked * contains Arabic (موجود) that is uncertain. The catchword "prium" is as printed. The Latin "mu'ltiplicitas" is printed with an apostrophe and is kept as printed. The bracketed "[Dei]" and "[vel per se]" are printed brackets.
